---
title: "Overview of Ecosystem Service: Physical Health (Hypertension)"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
    standalone: true
---

Urban greenspace is valued as the hypertension treatment cost it avoids. Greener urban
surroundings lower the odds of hypertension, so each city's greenness translates into avoided
cases among its adults, priced at the country's published cost of treating one case. The base
year is 2019.

Coverage is limited to the countries with a treatment-cost study (22, the updated cost table of
2 November 2026), by construction. Every other country carries NA with the absence named. The
counterfactual is a zero-vegetation city, which does much of the work in the magnitude, and the
whole avoided cost is attributed to greenspace.

## Source

The method is the authors' appendix of 22 October 2026, which is not yet in the shared folder
of current write-ups. The registered code, `libby-07/gep_health_hypertension` at `ac5c862`
(October 2025), predates it and differs in five ways: it uses the odds ratio directly, applies
adult prevalence to the whole population, measures greenness from Landsat at 500 m, prices in
international dollars and runs for the United States only. The library follows the appendix's
equations. Its costs are the updated table of 2 November 2026 (see Price), which replaces the
appendix's Table A1.

## Quantity

Per urban pixel on WorldPop's 1 km grid: population times annual NDVI (clamped at zero below),
summed per country over pixels inside the urban settlement mask
(`health_hypertension_urban_smod_min`). That sum, in 0.1-NDVI increments, times the WHO
hypertension prevalence among adults 30-79, times one minus the risk ratio, times the 30-79
population share, is the country's avoided cases. The risk ratio comes from the meta-analytic
odds ratio (`health_hypertension_odds_ratio`) converted at the country's own prevalence as the
baseline (Grant 2014).

## Price

The country's per-person hypertension cost in 2019 USD, one study per country, from the
physical-health team's updated cost table of 2 November 2026 (`ht_costs_uv.xlsx`, staged unchanged
with its provenance beside it). It covers 22 countries. Against the appendix's Table A1 it revises
15 of the 20 values by more than 5% and adds Cameroon and Pakistan. The cost is the total cost per
person where the study reports it, otherwise the direct cost per person, otherwise components of
the direct cost, and each row is converted to 2019 USD as the table's notes state. Mexico's
\$7,679.70 rests on the study's total cost of USD 6,020,017,806 at 14.85 MXN per USD over 749,701
cases in 2015, as its note states.

## Valuation

$$
\text{GEP}_i = c_i \; x_i \, \frac{\sum_{j \in \text{urban}} \text{NDVI}_j \, n_j}{0.1} \left(1 - \text{RR}_i\right) s_i
$$

with $c_i$ the treatment cost, $x_i$ the prevalence, $\text{RR}_i$ the converted risk ratio,
$s_i$ the 30-79 population share and $n_j$ the pixel population.

The appendix's own Table 6 is carried beside the result as the comparison anchor. It values 19
of the 22 countries (not Ghana, Cameroon or Pakistan) and totals \$104,664,962,067 at the Table A1
costs. At the updated costs the library is 0.90 times the reference over those 19, from 0.03
(Poland) to 18.9 (Mexico) times by country, because the two now price a case differently. At
matching costs the comparison is in avoided cases: the library's are 1.42 times those implied by
Table 6 and Table A1 in total, from 0.67 to 3.73 times by country.

A second column, `health_hypertension_gep_extended`, prices the same avoided cases in 187
countries. Where no study exists it transfers the cost from a regression of log cost on log GDP
per capita over the 22 studies (slope 0.56, R² 0.26, with Duan smearing 2.01), and it keeps the
observed cost where a study exists. It totals \$158,014,033,621.54 and is not the published value.

## Coverage

The published table is one row for each of the account's 250 countries, base year 2019, in 2019
USD. Of the 250, 22 carry a value, totalling \$94,425,983,075.38, 0 are computed zeros, and 228
rows are missing, kept as missing rather than zero because an input carries no data for those
countries. 169 of the 228 lack only a treatment cost, and the `note` column names what each
lacks. A zero means the computation returned zero. A missing row means the data to compute one
is absent.

## Inputs

All paths and parameters come from `es_parameters.csv` under the `health_hypertension` service
key: the WorldPop mosaic, the annual NDVI, the GHS-SMOD urban mask and its threshold, the WHO
prevalence, the 30-79 shares, the cost table, the odds ratio and the appendix reference, each
with a source row beside it.

## Output

`gep_calculation` writes `gep_by_country_base_year.csv` into its own task directory, holding the
r250 identifiers and attributes, `year`, `health_hypertension_gep`, the extended and reference
columns, and the inputs behind each value: the urban NDVI-weighted population, the prevalence,
the 30-79 share, the cost per case and its source, the avoided cases and a `note`.

## What is open

- Baseline prevalence. The appendix uses dense-urban prevalence or a study quantile. The
  library uses the national WHO prevalence among adults 30-79.
- Greenness exposure. The appendix measures NDVI from Landsat over a 500 m buffer. The library
  uses the MODIS 1 km annual mean per pixel.
- The gap to the appendix's Table 6 in avoided cases, 1.42 times at matching costs, is not
  reconciled. The library's final step and input joins are checked independently, and the
  rasters are not reproduced (open question 20).
